key_facts.fact: Exa raised a $250M Series C at a $2.2B valuation on May 20, 2026, led by a16z with Benchmark, Lightspeed and Y Combinator; reported 400,000+ developers and 5,000+ companies; Marcus Holm (ex-President of LaunchDarkly) joined as CRO.
Series B: $85M at $700M valuation led by Benchmark on Sep 3, 2025 (Lightspeed, YC, NVentures). Exa started in 2021 and in Sept 2025 described itself as having two products: the API and Websets.
Seed plus Series A totaled $22M, led by Lightspeed with NVentures and YC, announced July 16, 2024.
Exa was previously named Metaphor and rebranded on January 25, 2024.
Founders are Will Bryk (CEO, ex-Cresta) and Jeff Wang (co-founder, ex-Plaid); about page cites hundreds of H200 GPUs and a 500B+ page index.
As of August 2026 Exa's index tracks 1.4 trillion URLs and serves 100 billion pages; ExaSearchBot respects robots.txt and does not bypass logins, paywalls or CAPTCHAs.
Third-party revenue estimates only: Sacra estimated $10M ARR in Sept 2025 (about 11x YoY); ARR Club lists $12M ARR in January 2026. Exa has not published revenue.

NYC Forward Deployed Engineer posting (published Aug 13, 2026): in-person NYC, GTM department, $130K to $275K plus equity and bonus; FDE owns customers from cold outbound to production integration to closed deal; team size stated as about 100.

FDE EMEA/APJ postings define the FDE as paired with an AE to own the technical win: discovery, solution design, demos, POCs/POVs with clear success criteria, objection handling, security questionnaires and RFPs; AI-assisted coding expected.
Forward Deployed PM posting (Sep 26, 2026) says the team is about 150 people and the role builds proof-of-value demos and helps price custom engagements.

Technical Enablement Manager posting says enablement for FDEs centers on demo excellence and the POV/POC process, value narratives, technical objection handling, competitive positioning and demo scenarios across industries and personas.

Exa's enterprise page offers a demo where the prospect brings a query their current search gets wrong and Exa runs it live; lists forward-deployed engineers, custom data indexes, SLAs, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with BAA, ZDR; claims 500,000+ developers.

Changelog (Oct 2025 to Sep 2026): Deep search (Nov 20), People Search (Dec 19), Company Search (Jan 21), maxAgeHours replaces livecrawl (Feb 2), Exa Instant (Feb 5), pricing overhaul (Mar 3), deep-reasoning with field-level grounding (Mar 4), Monitors (Mar 30), /research retired (Apr 1), Exa Agent (Jun 16), Exa Connect (Jun 24), Agent in MCP (Jul 1), publication search 350M papers (Jul 23), Dynamic Highlights preview (Aug 28), Agent Ultra (Sep 24).
Websets docs now tell new list-building users to use Exa Agent and keep Websets for existing integrations.

Current list pricing: Search instant $4/1k, fast/auto $7/1k (10 results with text and highlights), Deep $12/1k, Deep-reasoning $15/1k, Contents $1/1k pages, Answer $5/1k, Monitors $15/1k, Agent $0.012 to $1.00 per fixed run or metered with $5/$20 caps; $10 free credits monthly.
ZDR is Enterprise-only, enabled per team, available for Search, Contents and Agent but not Answer or Websets.
HIPAA mode applies only to cached retrieval: /search with instant or fast type, text or highlights, no summaries, no live crawl.

Google's Grounding with Exa web search in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform requires the customer's own Exa API key, bills Exa usage at Exa's rates plus Gemini tokens, default quota 200 prompts per minute; page updated 2026-09-28.
Google added Parallel as a native grounding provider on July 16, 2026, purchasable through Google Cloud Marketplace on the existing Google invoice.
Nebius agreed to acquire Tavily on Feb 10, 2026; Tavily keeps its brand; Tavily has a 1M+ developer community and customers including IBM, Cohere and Groq.
Tavily deal reported at $275M upfront, up to $400M with milestones (citing Calcalist); Tavily had raised $25M.

Parallel Web Systems raised a $100M Series B at a $2B valuation led by Sequoia (Apr 29, 2026), five months after a $100M Series A at $740M; $230M total; 100,000+ developers; customers include Clay, Harvey, Notion, Opendoor.
Parallel's own Sep 9, 2026 BrowseComp comparison shows Parallel 74% at $399 per 1,000 questions vs Exa Auto 70% at $971, calling Exa the most expensive frontier run.

Independent AIMultiple benchmark (May 25, 2026, updated Sep 27, 2026; 100 queries, GPT-5.2 judge): Brave 14.89, Firecrawl 14.58, Exa 14.39, Parallel Pro 14.21, Tavily 13.67, Perplexity 12.96, SerpAPI 12.28; top four statistically tied; SerpApi disclosed as a subscriber.
Exa-run benchmarks vs Tavily (Aug 4, 2026): people rank-1 recall 75.5% vs 40.5%, company 81.5% vs 61.3%, publications 63.3% vs 31.8%; Tavily concedes higher published RPM and bundled raw content.
Exa's own Brave comparison concedes Brave's higher citation precision (0.328 vs 0.259) and cheaper list price ($5 vs $7 per 1,000), while claiming 2x lower latency and much better entity retrieval.
Brave Search API: Search $5 per 1,000 requests, Answers $4 per 1,000 plus $5 per million tokens, 50 QPS, 30B+ page independent index, ZDR; customers AWS, Shopify, Snowflake, Cohere, Mistral.

Perplexity Search API is $5 per 1,000 requests and $1 per 1,000 with Fast Search; Agent API web_search tool $2.50 per 1,000, people_search and finance_search $5 per 1,000; Perplexity now documents an MCP server.
Perplexity launched its Search API on Sep 26, 2025 at $5 per 1,000 requests, claiming an index of hundreds of billions of pages.

Grounding with Google Search on Gemini 3 costs $14 per 1,000 grounding queries after 5,000 free per month (billing began Jan 5, 2026); older models $35 per 1,000 prompts; Web Grounding for Enterprise $45 per 1,000 prompts.
Google's Custom Search JSON API is closed to new customers and existing customers must move off by January 1, 2027.
Bing Search APIs were retired August 11, 2025; Microsoft points customers to Grounding with Bing Search in Azure AI Agents.
Grounding with Bing costs $14 per 1,000 transactions, 150 TPS, and its output is restricted to use within Microsoft products such as Azure AI Foundry.
You.com raised a $100M Series C at $1.5B (Sep 3, 2025, led by Cox); over 1 billion API queries per month; customers DuckDuckGo, Windsurf, Harvey.
Linkup raised a $10M seed led by Gradient; offices in New York, SF and Paris; offers private index and bring-your-own-cloud, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA, ZDR; logos include KPMG, McKinsey, EY, Databricks.
Firecrawl raised a $75M Series B led by Smash Ventures on Sep 22, 2026 and launched the Alexandria data platform.
Google sued SerpApi on Dec 19, 2025 alleging circumvention of security measures to scrape and resell licensed content.
Per a third-party summary, the core Google v. SerpApi claims were dismissed July 20, 2026; Google refiled Aug 10 and SerpApi moved to dismiss again Aug 25.
Exa's April 2026 deprecation made startCrawlDate/endCrawlDate silently ignored from April 15 while still returning HTTP 200, flagged as a stale-data risk by a monitoring vendor's blog.
monday.com case study: 2.7M enrichments, 50% less research time per SDR/AE, top 10 leads pre-mapped in CRM on login.
CodeRabbit case study: Deep Search cut P50 latency to 7.1s from 30 to 45s and reduced web-search call volume 70 to 75%.
HubSpot case study: Exa beat native model search for HubSpot; 40% latency improvement; uses Search API and Monitors API.
Exa demo gallery includes Exa vs Native Search, GTM Intelligence (domain to TAM list, scored prospects, decision makers, monitors), Company and People Enrichment, voice agent, paper search.
Exa Snapshot pins search and contents to a stored page version at a chosen past datetime (rolling 5-month window) for backtests and reproducible evals.
Singapore office opened March 30, 2026 as Exa's first APAC office, focused on core retrieval engineering.

uncertainties: Exa's revenue is not public; the $10M (Sept 2025) and $12M (Jan 2026) ARR figures are third-party estimates from Sacra and ARR Club and could be well off, especially after the May 2026 raise.
Headcount conflicts across Exa's own postings: about 100 (FDE postings, Aug 2026) versus about 150 (Forward Deployed PM posting, Sep 26, 2026).

Index size and developer counts differ across Exa pages (500B+ pages vs 1.4T URLs tracked / 100B served; 400,000 vs 500,000 developers); latency for Exa Instant ranges from sub-150ms to 323ms depending on the page.

Nearly all head-to-head benchmark numbers are vendor-run (Exa's versus pages, Parallel's article). The only independent benchmark found (AIMultiple) discloses SerpApi as a subscriber and shows the top four providers statistically tied.

Exa's comparison pages are partly stale: the Perplexity page (Feb 2026) says Perplexity has no MCP server or people search, but Perplexity's current docs show both; Feb/Mar 2026 pages quote Exa at $5 per 1,000, not the current $4/$7.
Default data retention for non-ZDR Exa accounts is not stated on any page I read; I did not load trust.exa.ai.
Launch dates for Exa Snapshot, Batch API, Exa in Slack, Exa for Google Sheets and HIPAA mode are not in the changelog.

Whether Grounding with Exa in Google's platform is still private preview or generally available is unclear; the Exa blog (Apr 2026) said private preview and the Google doc page does not state a stage.
Series C angel investors (Scott Wu, Igor Babuschkin, Tal Broda) come from a search-result summary of press coverage, not a page I loaded directly.
Linkup's seed date differs between sources (FinSMEs Feb 2026 vs Linkup blog March 3, 2026). Tavily's deal price comes from SiliconANGLE citing Calcalist; Nebius did not disclose it.
The status of Google v. SerpApi after Aug 25, 2026 comes from a third-party blog (CrawlRaven), not court records.
What the Oct 2 demo round is testing is my inference from the recruiter brief and Exa's postings; Exa has published nothing about its FDE interview loop.

checks.claim: 17. HIPAA mode applies only to cached retrieval: /search with instant or fast type, text or highlights, no summaries, no live crawl.
checks.correction: HIPAA mode covers BOTH /search and /contents, not just /search. It is switched on per request with a top-level field "compliance": "hipaa", only for Enterprise teams Exa has enabled (otherwise 403 FEATURE_DISABLED). On /search, type must be explicitly instant or fast (omitting type is rejected); on /contents, omit freshness fields or set maxAgeHours: -1. No summary on either. Incompatible requests return 400 INVALID_REQUEST_BODY. HIPAA mode includes ZDR for those requests; other endpoints (Answer, Agent, Monitors) reject the field.

Parameters that now fail silently. The report mentions startCrawlDate/endCrawlDate only through a third-party blog. The changelog says that since Jul 23, 2026 they are 'ignored for all teams' while still being accepted. It also says: livecrawl is replaced by maxAgeHours (0 = always crawl, -1 = cache only); highlights numSentences and highlightsPerUrl are deprecated in favor of highlights.maxCharacters; the 'linkedin' category became 'people'; 'research paper' became 'publication'; and the pdf, github and tweet categories are being deprecated. Old tutorial code will return HTTP 200 with quietly wrong behavior. Source: https://exa.ai/docs/changelog.md

Current parameter names a demo would use: type (instant, fast, auto, deep-lite, deep, deep-reasoning); category ('company', 'people', 'publication'); outputSchema (returns output.content plus output.grounding, which are field-level citations); includeDomains/excludeDomains (supports paths and *.subdomain wildcards); userLocation; snapshotAsOf. Agent API: POST /agent/runs with effort (minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, auto, ultra), outputSchema, input.data, dataSources for Connect, budget.maxCostDollars and budget.maxDurationSeconds, plus POST /agent/runs/{id}/stop. Dynamic Highlights (a research preview) needs dynamic: true plus the header 'Exa-Beta: dynamic-highlights-2026-08-28'. Sources: https://exa.ai/docs/changelog.md, https://exa.ai/docs/admin/pricing.md

Named customer quotes with job titles on the enterprise page, useful for the slides: Daniel Lereya (Chief Product and Technology Officer, monday.com), Praty Sharma (AI Lead, HubSpot), Walden Yan (Co-founder, Cognition), David Loker (VP of AI, CodeRabbit), Alex Atallah (CEO, OpenRouter), Prabhav Jain (CEO, 11x). The page also claims 'Up to 94% fewer tokens per answer' and shows an Exa-run latency chart: Exa Instant 45% / 178 ms, Parallel 37% / 3051 ms, Brave 20% / 559 ms, Tavily Ultra-Fast 11% / 260 ms. The scraped text did not say what the percentage axis measures. Source: https://exa.ai/enterprise

Exa gives several different latency numbers for Instant: 'sub-150ms' in the changelog (Feb 5, 2026), 'under 180 ms' on the enterprise page, and 'sub200ms' in the Series C blog. In a live pitch, quote one number and name its page.

Launch dates the report said it could not find. Exa Snapshot came out Sep 17, 2026 ('Introducing Exa Snapshot, A New Way to Search the Past'), and the Agent Ultra blog is dated Sep 25, 2026 (changelog says Sep 24). Both appear in the 'See more' list at the bottom of https://exa.ai/blog/announcing-series-c

Snapshot limits that matter for a finance backtest demo. Pay-as-you-go runs at 10 QPS (queries per second) with a rolling 5-month window, and after 100 requests you must talk to sales. On /search, snapshotAsOf goes inside 'contents', not at the top level. Source: https://exa.ai/docs/search/snapshot.md
Websets API needs a paid Websets plan, and Websets credits are separate from Search API credits. Free plan caps a webset at 25 verified results. Source: https://exa.ai/docs/websets/quickstart.md

Google's Exa grounding tool details, relevant if the enterprise story runs through Google Cloud. SDK tool is types.Tool(exa_ai_search=types.ToolExaAiSearch(api_key=..., custom_configs={...})). Only 'fast' and 'instant' search types are allowed. numResults defaults to 5. includeDomains/excludeDomains accept up to 1200 domains. Supported models include gemini-2.5-flash/pro and gemini-3.5-flash. Google calls it a 'Separate Offering' under the Google Cloud Agreement. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/models/grounding/grounding-with-exa
